'''Nicola Pinna''' (born 14 November 1974 in [[Milan]], [[Italy]]) is a [[chemist]] and professor at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]].

== Scientific career ==
Pinna's doctoral studies were undertaken at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] ([[Paris]]) with a focus on physical chemistry. His [[postdoctoral]] work at [[Fritz Haber Institute of the MPG]] ([[Berlin]]) saw him researching the catalytic properties of vanadium oxide nanoparticles. He has since worked at the [[Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces]] ([[Potsdam]]), [[Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg]], the [[University of Aveiro]] (Portugal), and [[Seoul National University]] (Korea). He has been a professor of inorganic chemistry at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] since July 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nicola Pinna|url=http://www.pinna.info/|accessdate=2015-11-28}}</ref> From July 2016 to April 2021 he was also head of the Department of Chemistry.<ref>{{cite web|title=Institute of Chemistry of the Humboldt University of Berlin|url=https://www.chemie.hu-berlin.de/en/department-en/standardseite?set_language=en|accessdate=2017-10-03}}</ref>

His research focuses on nanostructured materials, mainly dealing with the synthesis of nanomaterials by solution and gas phase routes, their characterization and the study of their physical properties. In particular, his research interests include the synthesis of crystalline [[Oxide|metal oxide]] [[nanoparticle]]s, [[Heterojunction|heterostructures]], [[hybrid material]]s and [[thin film]]s by novel nonaqueous [[sol-gel]] routes, their assembly, and the study of their physical properties such as optical, electrical, electrochemical, magnetic, catalytic, and gas sensing.

In 2011, he was ranked among the top 100 materials scientists of the past decade by impact.<ref>{{cite web|title=Top 100 materials scientists|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/dr/sci/misc/Top100MatSci2000-10|accessdate=2015-02-21}}</ref>

He is executive editor of the ''[[Journal of Nanoparticle Research]]'',<ref>{{cite web|title=Journal of Nanoparticle Research - Editorial Board|url=https://www.springer.com/materials/nanotechnology/journal/11051?detailsPage=editorialBoard|accessdate=2015-02-21}}</ref> associate editor of Carbon Energy,<ref>{{cite web|title=Carbon Energy - Editorial Board|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/26379368/homepage/editorial-board|accessdate=2025-02-06}}</ref> EcoEnergy<ref>{{cite web|title=EcoEnergy - Editorial Board|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/28359399/homepage/editorial-board|accessdate=2025-02-05}}</ref> and was member of the editorial board of the Journal [[CrystEngComm]] from 2011 to 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=CrystEngComm - Editorial Staff|url=http://www.rsc.org/Publishing/Journals/ce/Staff.asp|accessdate=2015-02-21}}</ref> Additionally he published books on [[Atomic Layer Deposition]]<ref>{{cite book|last1=Knez|first1=Mato|last2=Pinna|first2=Nicola|title=Atomic Layer Deposition of Nanostructured Materials|date=2012|publisher=Wiley-VCH|isbn=9783527327973|doi=10.1002/9783527639915}}</ref> and the synthesis of [[nanoparticle]]s.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Niederberger|first1=Markus|last2=Pinna|first2=Nicola|title=Metal Oxide Nanoparticles in Organic Solvents|date=2009|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-1-84882-671-7|url=https://www.springer.com/materials/mechanics/book/978-1-84882-670-0}}</ref>
